title: Jeremy Corners
author: Isaac Banner
notes: The Caller's Box 20362, permission: full. The author's own note: "Author recommends you not call this dance." And the one that decides how it is encoded: "Square through is done in a diamond formation." A two-pass record, the second pass the same with the twos active; the set progresses at the end of each pass, which is what makes the second pass's own selections the next neighbour along. **The square through's foursome is written out** (M9b, DD31): `"who": "self+partner+N1+N2"`, the written relation list `docs/dance-record.md` now documents, is the transcript's "[with twos, W1, and N2 M1]" - four dancers named one at a time and out of two minor sets, which no tag, station list or single relation could say. Both passes write it, so the second pass's `[with N2]` is the same four one progression along. **Measured before and after, and it changes none of the gated oracles**: closure passes at 2, 4 and 6 couples and fails at **37.7359 px** at 3 and 5 either way, reach passes at every length either way, and collision fails at **0.000 px** at every length either way. The one number it does move is `progressed`, 32.0000 -> 37.7359 px at 2 couples. **Still owed, two things, both measured.** (a) Closure **37.7359 px** at the odd line lengths (3 and 5 couples), and M9b's measurement says it is **not** the square through: the worst seam is `c0/robin` at beat 192, `wait-out -> diamond` - a waiting couple coming back in, one place off where the diamond's cast expects it. An odd duple improper line has one waiting couple rather than two and the crossing lands it a place out; the even lengths close at 0.0000. (b) Collision **0.000 px** at every length, `c0/lark ~ c0/robin` at **beat 56** - inside B2's single-file promenade, where the ones' robin is the one dancer of the four the transcript leaves out (`who: ["1L", "2L", "2R"]`) and stands where the ones' lark walks through. **Two readings still unsettled by measurement.** (1) The second token of "Square through 2 (NR;SRNL)" could not be read. The first is a neighbour by the right; the second is written here as the partner by the left, because a square through's second hand is with somebody other than the first and a partner is who that is in a diamond. (2) "Ones turn contra corners (along the set)" is `axis: "along"`, which swaps which corner is first. `axis: "across"` was measured too and closes at 32.0000 px at 2, 4 and 6 couples against 37.7359 at 3 and 5, so the transcript's own word is kept and the other reading is a pixel or two better at half the line lengths. Neither changes the motion: `turn-contra-corners` runs a hand at **297.4 px/beat** against a bound of 68.4 either way, because after the diamond the actives are standing in the middle of the set and their corners are a whole dancing place and a half away.

source.transcript:
A1  (8) Ones pass through across (1R); turn right; cast clockwise around one; step into center and face partner in distance; form diamonds  (8) Interrupted square through 2 [with twos, W1, and N2 M1]: (4) Neighbor balance (RH)  (4) Square through 2 (NR;SRNL)
A2  (16) Ones turn contra corners (along the set)
B1  (4) Ones balance  (12) Ones swing; face down
B2  (4) Balance ring  (4) [Man one and twos] Single file promenade clockwise 1/3  (8) Neighbor swing
2A1-2B2: the same with the twos active, [with N2]/[N3] selections.
Author recommends you _not_ call this dance. Square through is done in a diamond formation.
